claim: The Claude Code team officially defines loops as 'agents repeating cycles of work until a stop condition is met,' categorized by trigger mechanism, stop criteria, which Claude Code primitive is used, and the most appropriate task type.
stance_target: canonical definition of agentic loops for triggers/infrastructure architecture (Pillar 5)
quoted_support: On the Claude Code team, we define loops as agents repeating cycles of work until a stop condition is met.

claim: The /goal primitive's independent evaluator model checks a user-defined stop condition every time Claude attempts to end the loop, specifically to prevent the agent from self-determining that its own work is 'good enough.'
quoted_support: When you define the success criteria, Claude doesn't have to make a determination on what is "good enough" and end the loop early. Each time Claude tries to stop, an evaluator model checks your condition and sends it back to work until the goal is met or a number of turns you define is reached.

claim: Anthropic officially recommends routing proactive/scheduled loop work to smaller, faster models while reserving the most capable model for judgment calls -- a direct cost-optimization pattern for continuous agentic operation.
stance_target: cost and resource optimization for always-on agent fleets (Pillar 6)
scope_conditions: official Claude Code guidance on proactive loops, 2026
quoted_support: Managed usage by: Routing routines to smaller, faster models and using the most capable model for judgment calls.

claim: Anthropic's official guidance recommends using a second agent with fresh context (not the agent that wrote the code) for code review, because such a reviewer 'is less biased and not influenced by the main agent's reasoning,' and explicitly frames this as part of a broader principle that 'loops that write code need loops that check it.'
quoted_support: Use a second agent for code reviews: A reviewer with fresh context is less biased and not influenced by the main agent's reasoning... Loops that write code need loops that check it.

claim: Anthropic warns that dynamic workflows can spawn hundreds of agents simultaneously, and recommends piloting on a smaller slice of work before a large run to gauge token/cost usage.
stance_target: cost control and auto-killing idle/runaway agent fleets (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: Pilot before a large run: Dynamic workflows can spawn hundreds of agents. Gauge usage on a smaller slice of the work first.

claim: Claude Code exposes real-time cost observability commands: /usage breaks down recent usage by skills, subagents, and MCPs; /goal (no arguments) shows turn count and token usage so far; /workflows shows each agent's token usage and allows stopping any agent at any time.
stance_target: infrastructure for monitoring and killing agents to control cost (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: The /usage command breaks down recent usage by skills, subagents, and MCPs, /goal with no arguments shows number of turns and token usage so far, /workflows shows each agent's token usage and you can stop an agent at any time.
